title: Organizing: which product, which heading, which role
blurb: Match named people to board, assurance and team roles, and place organizing information in the right product and commercial management approach heading.
question: Brennan Mutual's cloud partner Stratoshift will carry out most of the migrations while the society's own IT staff decommission the hardware. Under which commercial management approach heading does this belong?

teach.h: Who, in which role, written where
teach.body: Formally, the organizing practice defines and establishes the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities. Its management products are the project management team structure, the role descriptions and the commercial management approach, all part of the PID. In plain English: who is involved and how they relate, what each role must do, and how the project buys and manages outside help. Practitioner items ask you to fit named people to roles and facts to products or headings.

head: Product
Holds
rows: Who is involved, relationships, ways of working
How commercial agreements are secured and run
teach.caption: All three are created or completed in initiation as part of the PID and are reviewed at stage boundaries and in closing.

head: Heading
Holds
Project Skyline example
rows: People and means for that work
teach.caption: These three headings are confirmed by the official sample rationales. Delivery models range from thin client (suppliers do most work, even much project management) to thick client (the business does most work).

levels.label: Directing
levels.sub: Project board: executive, senior user, senior supplier

levels.label: Delivering
levels.sub: Team managers such as Arjun Menon

teach.caption: The project management team is the three lower levels; the business layer sits outside it and appoints the executive.

teach.h: Role fit: what to look for
head: Role
Good fit
Red flag
rows: Budget holder who can secure funding
Heads the people who use the outputs
No stake in using the outputs
Leads the team doing the work
teach.caption: The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of products delivered by suppliers and the technical integrity of the project (6.2.4.3).

teach.body: In starting up, the business layer is accountable and the executive responsible for appointing the executive and the project manager, and for appointing the rest of the project management team; the project manager is not involved in those appointments. The project board decides how project assurance will be done. Project support is the project manager's responsibility and can be delegated, for example to a PMO or supplier, but must stay separate from assurance.

teach.text: Two traps. The project board directs; the project management team structure is only a description of roles and has no authority of its own. And PRINCE2 has no 'sponsor' role: a sponsor usually becomes, or sits above, the executive.

teach.body: Fraser McIntyre, the chief operating officer and IT budget holder, fits the executive role. Joanne Pettigrew, whose branch and contact centre teams use most of the applications, fits senior user. Lena Fischer, who commits Stratoshift's people and answers for their quality, fits senior supplier; Arjun Menon, who leads the engineers, is a team manager. Mairi Campbell is project manager. Victoria Sharma's risk function, independent of Mairi, could provide business assurance.

items: Read each person's background in the Additional Information and in the stem.
Executive: senior, holds or can secure the budget, accountable for value.
Senior user: heads the people who will use or operate the outputs and realize benefits.
Senior supplier: can commit the supplier's people and answers for product quality.
Assurance: independent of the PM; never the PM, a team member or project support.
Organizing products: PMT structure, role descriptions, commercial management approach (6.5).
Commercial headings confirmed: responsibilities, resources, delivery model.
Role descriptions include accountability for sustainability targets.
SU appointments: business layer accountable, executive responsible, PM not involved.
Project support can be delegated but is kept separate from project assurance.

summary: You can now fit named people to the executive, senior user, senior supplier, assurance and team manager roles. You can place organizing facts in the PMT structure, role descriptions or the right commercial management approach heading.

A.q: Brennan Mutual's Project Skyline will move about 140 applications to the cloud. Candidates for executive are: Fraser McIntyre, chief operating officer and budget holder for IT and operations; Aileen Docherty, chief information officer, who reports to him; Joanne Pettigrew, head of member services; and Lena Fischer, engagement director at the cloud partner. Who is most appropriate as executive?
A.why: The executive is the single point of accountability and secures funding. Fraser holds the IT and operations budget and is senior enough to own the business case (6.2.4.1).

whyNot.0: Aileen reports to Fraser and does not hold the budget; she also wants extra scope, which the executive must judge.
whyNot.2: Joanne's teams use the applications, which makes her a natural senior user.
whyNot.3: Lena represents the supplier, so she fits senior supplier, not executive.

A.q: On Brennan Mutual's Project Skyline, the cloud partner Stratoshift will do most of the migration work. Its people include Lena Fischer, engagement director, who commits Stratoshift's staff and is accountable for the quality of its work, and Arjun Menon, delivery lead, who leads twelve engineers in Pune. Who should be senior supplier for Stratoshift?
A.why: The senior supplier commits supplier people and resources and is accountable for the quality of supplier products (6.2.4.3). Lena does both.

whyNot.1: Arjun leads the engineers doing the work, which fits a team manager role.
whyNot.2: Steven, the society's enterprise architect, cannot commit Stratoshift's staff.
whyNot.3: Nicola manages supplier contracts for the society; she cannot commit Stratoshift's people.

A.q: Brennan Mutual is writing Project Skyline's commercial management approach. It states that Stratoshift will build the cloud landing zone and carry out most application migrations, the core banking vendor will move its own system, and the society's IT staff will remove the old hardware. Where should this be recorded?
A.why: The delivery model heading describes how the project work will be delivered, for example which elements of the WBS external suppliers deliver (6.5, 6.3.2.1).

whyNot.0: Responsibilities cover who does market engagement, procurement and contract management.
whyNot.1: Resources cover the people and means for those commercial activities.
whyNot.3: The PMT structure shows who is involved and how they relate, not which parts of the work each supplier delivers.

B.q: Project Skyline's commercial management approach must record that Nicola Graham, the society's supplier management lead, will make the regulatory notifications about the outsourcing and manage the Stratoshift and core banking vendor contracts. Where should this be recorded?
B.why: The responsibilities heading defines who is responsible for market engagement, procurement and contract management activities (6.5).

whyNot.0: The delivery model describes which parts of the work suppliers deliver, not who manages the contracts.
whyNot.1: Resources describe the people and means provided for commercial work, not the named responsibilities.
whyNot.3: The issue management approach covers how issues and changes to baselines are handled, not commercial responsibilities.

B.q: Brennan Mutual's board for Project Skyline wants business assurance, independent of project manager Mairi Campbell, on whether the business case remains valid. Mairi suggests her project support officer, who already maintains the registers, could do it. Who is most appropriate?
B.why: Project assurance must be independent of the PM and cannot be done by the PM, project team members or project support (6.2.4.7). Victoria leads an independent risk function.

whyNot.0: The project manager cannot perform project assurance.
whyNot.1: Project support must be kept separate from project assurance to protect its independence.
whyNot.2: Arjun works for the supplier and leads the migration work, so he cannot give the board an independent business view of the business case.

B.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. Fraser McIntyre has been appointed executive. The senior user and senior supplier now need to be appointed. Which role should be responsible for appointing them?
B.why: In 'appoint the project management team' the executive is responsible and the business layer accountable; the project manager is not involved (13.4.4).

whyNot.0: The project manager is not involved in appointing the project management team.
whyNot.2: The business layer is accountable for the appointments; the executive is responsible for making them.
whyNot.3: The senior user is one of the roles being appointed.

C.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell, the project manager, writes the role descriptions, including in each team manager's description their accountability for the sustainability targets in their work, such as certified data destruction and responsible disposal of old hardware. Is this an appropriate application of the 'organizing' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because role descriptions include accountability for sustainability targets
Yes, because team managers set tolerances for the members of their team
No, because sustainability targets are documented in the sustainability approach
No, because team managers sit outside the project management team structure
C.why: Role descriptions set out the specific responsibilities of each role, including accountability for sustainability targets (6.5).

whyNot.1: It is true that team managers set tolerances for team members, but that does not explain why sustainability accountability belongs in role descriptions.
whyNot.2: Targets are documented in the sustainability approach, but who is accountable for them is also stated in role descriptions.
whyNot.3: Team managers are part of the project management team structure, at the delivering level.

C.q: Project Skyline is planning its decommissioning stage. Fraser McIntyre proposes that Mairi Campbell, the project manager, also acts as team manager for the society's small in-house decommissioning team, because she has led similar work and has capacity in that stage. Is this an appropriate application of the 'organizing' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because the project manager role should not be shared with others
Yes, because skill and capacity allow the PM to also be team manager
No, because a team manager for supplier work must come from the supplier
No, because the project manager cannot hold a second project role
C.why: Depending on scale, complexity, skill and capacity, the project manager may also perform the team manager and project support roles (6.2.4.5).

whyNot.0: It is true the PM role should not be shared, but combining it with the team manager role is not sharing it.
whyNot.2: This is in-house work, and team managers can come from the business or a supplier.
whyNot.3: The PM may also hold the team manager and project support roles.

C.q: Brennan Mutual's last IT project ended in a dispute over what had been agreed. For Project Skyline, the supplier management lead proposes that the commercial management approach states which elements of the work breakdown structure Stratoshift and the core banking vendor will each deliver. Is this an appropriate application of the 'organizing' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because the PMT structure shows the relationships between parties
Yes, because the delivery model sets out which work suppliers deliver
No, because supplier scope is agreed in each work package description
No, because commercial agreements are made by the business layer
C.why: The commercial management approach's delivery model describes the delivery model for the project work, including the WBS elements delivered by external suppliers (6.5).

whyNot.0: The PMT structure shows relationships, but that does not explain recording which work each supplier delivers.
whyNot.2: Work package descriptions pass specific work to teams, but the overall split of work between suppliers is set in the delivery model.
whyNot.3: The commercial management approach covers how the project secures and manages its commercial agreements.

reteach.title: A cast list, a script and a contract file
reteach.question: If the project were a theatre production, which document is the cast list, which is the script for each part, and which is the contract file?

blocks.body: The PMT structure is the cast list: who is in the project, how they relate and how they will work together. Role descriptions are each actor's script: responsibilities, authority and accountability, including for sustainability targets. The commercial management approach is the contract file: who handles engagement, buying and contracts, what resources they have, and which parts of the work each supplier delivers.

blocks.h: Where does this organizing fact go?

blocks.text: The person who leads the supplier's engineers is usually a team manager; the person who can commit the supplier's people and answer for their quality is the senior supplier.

explain.body: The PMT structure shows who is involved, their relationships and how they will work together. Role descriptions give each role's specific responsibilities, including accountability for sustainability targets.

test.q: Mairi Campbell needs to record, for Project Skyline, a chart showing the project board, herself, the team managers, project assurance and project support, and the lines of authority between them. Which product should hold this?
test.why: The PMT structure shows who is involved, their relationships and how they will work together (6.5).

whyNot.0: The communication approach covers the means and frequency of communication with stakeholders.
whyNot.1: Role descriptions describe each role's responsibilities, not the overall structure.
whyNot.2: The commercial approach covers commercial agreements.

explain.body: It describes procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities for securing, servicing and maintaining commercial agreements: market engagement, procurement and contract management. Confirmed headings: responsibilities, resources and delivery model.

test.q: Brennan Mutual will lend two procurement specialists to Project Skyline for three months to agree terms with Stratoshift. Where should this be recorded?
test.why: The resources heading covers the resources for market engagement, procurement and contract management (6.5).

whyNot.0: Responsibilities name who is responsible for the activities, not the people provided as resources.
whyNot.1: The delivery model describes which work suppliers deliver.
whyNot.3: Role descriptions cover project management team roles; resources lent for procurement are a commercial approach entry.

explain.body: Executive: secures funding, owns the business case; one only, never combined with the PM. Senior user: represents users, specifies benefits, handover and adoption. Senior supplier: commits supplier resources, accountable for supplier product quality and technical integrity.

test.q: Project Skyline's branch and contact centre staff use most of the applications being moved. Joanne Pettigrew, head of member services, manages them. Which role best suits Joanne?
test.why: The senior user represents those who will use the products and specifies the benefits (6.2.4.2).

whyNot.0: Joanne does not supply the products.
whyNot.1: Fraser McIntyre holds the budget; there can be only one executive.
whyNot.2: Joanne's area is directly affected, so she is a user representative rather than an independent assurer.

explain.body: The board decides how project assurance is done; it may use people from the business or external parties, but never the PM, team members or project support. Project support is the PM's responsibility and can be delegated, but must stay separate from assurance.

test.q: On Project Skyline, Mairi Campbell wants the society's project management office to keep the registers, run version control and organize board meetings. Which role does this describe?
test.why: Project support provides administrative services, registers and version control; it is the PM's responsibility and can be delegated to a PMO (6.2.4).

whyNot.1: Project assurance checks the project for the board, independently of the PM.
whyNot.2: A team manager delivers specialist products.
whyNot.3: A change authority approves changes within delegated limits.
